obligations.statement: OpenAI's permanent construction yields a square polynomial map F0:C^k->C^k of degree d-1 with F0^{-1}(0)={0}, hence a fibre with (d-1)^k distinct simple points.
Baur-Strassen applies over the rational-function field and computes f and all first partial derivatives with at most three times the nonscalar multiplication/division complexity.
obligations.source: Baur-Strassen 1983, Theorem 1 (and Theorem 2 for operation-count refinement)

obligations.statement: A valid rational circuit with q nonlinear multiplication/division gates whose polynomial output fibre contains M isolated points in the circuit regularity domain satisfies M <= 2^q.
obligations.basis: quadratic multiplication/division graph equations plus the same isolated-solution affine Bezout bound used in OpenAI Lemma 4.1

obligations.statement: For each nonzero ambient numerator/denominator polynomial p, translations t for which p(Bu+c0+t) vanishes identically form a proper Zariski-closed set; finitely many such sets can be avoided by arbitrarily small t.
The (d-1)^k distinct simple fibre points persist as distinct simple local branches under sufficiently small translation.
obligations.basis: holomorphic implicit/inverse function theorem applied independently at the finitely many simple roots

obligations.statement: After a pole-avoiding translation, the pole locus Z has dimension at most k-1 and the Zariski closure of G(Z) has dimension at most k-1; therefore a nearby target avoids every pole while retaining all (d-1)^k simple local preimages.
obligations.basis: hypersurface dimension plus Stacks Project Lemma 33.20.4 componentwise

obligations.statement: O2-O6 imply (d-1)^k <= 2^(3s), hence s >= k log2(d-1)/3.
OpenAI's explicit parameters give k >= n^2/48 and log2(d-1) >= log2(log2 n)-3 for n>=2^16, yielding the coefficient 1/144.
As of 2026-08-14, the current OpenAI paper expressly excludes circuits with division and a fresh primary-source search located no theorem matching this valid-division extension.
